public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# TxGraffiti Conjecture 3: independent domination versus saturation (regular)

*Reference:* [arxiv/2507.17780](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17780)
**In Reverie Together: Ten Years of Mathematical Discovery with a Machine
Collaborator** by *Randy Davila, Boris Brimkov, Ryan Pepper*

Conjecture 3 (open since 2020) asserts that for every $r$-regular graph $G$
(every vertex has degree $r$),
$$i(G) \le \mu^*(G),$$
where $i(G)$ is the independent domination number and $\mu^*(G)$ the saturation
number (minimum size of a maximal matching).
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace Arxiv.«2507.17780»

/--
TxGraffiti [Conjecture 3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17780):
for every $r$-regular graph $G$ ($r \ge 1$),
$$i(G) \le \mu^*(G).$$

This conjecture is **open**.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem tx_graffiti_conjecture_3 (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (r : ℕ) (_hReg : ∀ v, G.degree v = r) (_hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    G.indepDominationNumber ≤ G.saturationNumber := by
  sorry

end Arxiv.«2507.17780»

findings.description: The module docstring (lines 27–29) states the inequality for every r-regular graph without requiring r > 0. This includes nonempty edgeless graphs: K₁ is 0-regular but has independent domination number 1 and saturation number 0. The theorem itself and its own docstring correctly include the positive-degree hypothesis, so the formal mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Davila–Brimkov–Pepper, arXiv:2507.17780, §3.3, Conjecture 3: “If G is an r-regular graph G with r > 0, then i(G) ≤ μ*(G), and this bound is sharp.” https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17780; downloaded LaTeX main.tex, lines 316–322.
findings.suggested_fix: Add “with r > 0” (or “r ≥ 1”) to the module summary at lines 27–28. No change to the theorem is needed.

reformulations.difference: The source defines i(G) using maximal independent sets; the Lean definition minimizes over independent dominating sets. The matching definition expresses maximality by prohibiting a single-edge extension.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An independent dominating set cannot be enlarged while remaining independent. Conversely, any vertex not dominated by an independent set can be added to it, so a maximal independent set is dominating. For matchings, the matching property is hereditary under taking subsets, making single-edge nonextendibility equivalent to inclusion-maximality. Both families have witnesses in every finite graph, so the natural-number infima are genuine attained minima. These equivalences, including the resulting inequality equivalence, were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2507.17780 — LaTeX source, particularly §3.3, Conjecture 3, its surrounding definitions and remarks, and the appendix
Local Mathlib: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Basic.lean, Clique.lean, Finite.lean, and Order/Lattice/Nat.lean
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the paper's Conjecture 3. Its quantifiers, finite simple-graph domain, regularity hypothesis, positive-degree bound, and inequality direction agree with the source. The cited paper still labels it open. Lean checks verified the existence of both minimizers and a computable companion for independent domination. Boundary tests gave (i, μ*) = (0,0) for the empty graph, (1,0) for the excluded singleton, (1,1) for K₂, (2,2) for 2K₂, and (3,3) for K₃,₃; small complete graphs and cycles were also tested. All experiments are under /workspace/review/.
